newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails three dissidents -- rights group.
newsitem.headline: China jails three dissidents -- rights group.

text.p: Chinese authorities have jailed two pro-democracy activists and sent another to a labour camp as part of a nationwide crackdown on dissent, a U.S.-based human rights watchdog said on Friday.

A court in central China's Anhui province had sentenced activist Shen Liangqing to 17 months in prison for counter- revolutionary propaganda and incitement and had jailed his associate Huang Xiuming for a year, Human Rights in China said.

In western Sichuan province, officials ordered veteran activist Wang Ming to serve three years of "re-education through labour" -- an administrative punishment that can be imposed without trial, the group said in a statement issued from its headquarters in New York.

Public security officials in Sichuan's Chongqing city declined to comment on Wang's case. Court officials in the Anhui capital Hefei -- who earlier confirmed Huang and Shen were on trial -- also declined to comment.

Human Rights in China said the two Anhui activists and a third, Ma Lianggang, had been charged on the basis of articles written and distributed in 1991 for which all three had already been detained for more than a year.
Ma had not been sentenced to a prison term but was stripped of his political rights for three years, the human rights group said.
All three of the Anhui dissidents were currently unemployed. Shen had been a government official, Huang a company manager and Ma a student.

Officials in Sichuan sent factory worker and veteran dissident Wang Ming to a labour camp for three years after he issued a public appeal for freedom of speech and called for the release of jailed activists, Human Rights in China said.
The 36-year-old veteran of 1979 Democracy Wall protests in Beijing was being held at one of the province's toughest labour camps, the group said.
China has in recent months detained or jailed a number of the nation's leading dissidents, dealing a series of blows to its tiny pro-democracy movement.
